contract: rebalance(state) -> array of N target weights, or None to keep the current shares. Called at weeks 145, 158, ..., 288 (every 13 weeks) for each OR-Library market: Hang Seng (N = 31), DAX 100 (85), FTSE 100 (89), S&P 100 (98), Nikkei 225 (225). state = {'week': t, 'index_prices': (t+1,) weekly index levels for weeks 0..t, 'stock_prices': (t+1, N), 'holdings': (N,) shares held, 'portfolio_value': value before trading, 'K': 10, 'min_weight': 0.01, 'max_weight': 1.0, 'cost_rate': 0.01, 'rebalance_every': 13}. Weights: at most 10 stocks held (|w| <= 1e-12 counts as not held), each held weight in [0.01, 1], summing to 1; a portfolio is required at week 145. The first purchase is free, later trades pay 1% of the traded value, and shares are held fixed between rebalances. Score: out-of-sample tracking error, the root-mean-square difference between weekly log returns of the portfolio (net of costs) and of the index over weeks 146..290, in percent, averaged over the five markets (minimize). The candidate runs in a separate sandboxed process: numpy, scipy, scikit-learn and the other installed packages are importable, while the evaluator's library, its data files, the network and subprocesses are not accessible; one thread and 3 GB of memory. It receives only the arguments described here, one call at a time: the arguments of a call are sent after the value of the previous call has been received. Arguments and return values travel as numbers, strings, lists, dicts with string keys and numeric numpy arrays, so a tuple arrives as a list
notes: Index tracking of Beasley, Meade and Chang (2003) on their five OR-Library markets: buy-and-hold positions in at most K = 10 stocks (holdings 1% to 100%), the first 145 weeks as the estimation period and the last 145 weeks for out-of-sample evaluation, root-mean-square tracking error of weekly log returns (their alpha = 2), proportional transaction costs of 1%. Deviations: optional rebalancing every 13 weeks with costs charged to the portfolio value (instead of their single rebalance with a cost budget and their excess-return trade-off), a free initial purchase and an at-most-K constraint. No published number is reproduced. Local references: the correlation/NNLS buy-and-hold seed 1.087; greedy forward selection on 104 weeks refreshed every 26 weeks 0.764.

name: Finance: Index tracking with few stocks and transaction costs (OR-Library)
description: Track five stock indices (Hang Seng, DAX 100, FTSE 100, S&P 100 and Nikkei 225) with buy-and-hold positions in at most ten constituents, formed from the first 145 weeks of prices and optionally rebalanced every 13 weeks at a 1% cost. The evaluator recomputes the portfolio values and scores the out-of-sample tracking error over the last 145 weeks.
benchmark: Finance: Index tracking with few stocks and transaction costs (OR-Library)
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Beasley, Meade and Chang (2003): index tracking with buy-and-hold positions in at most K stocks, holding bounds, transaction costs, tracking error (sum of |portfolio - index log return|^alpha / T)^(1/alpha), and the five OR-Library markets.
Canakgoz and Beasley (2009): mixed-integer programming approaches for index tracking on the same OR-Library data.
OR-Library indtrack1-indtrack5 (weekly prices of the index and its constituents, weeks 0-290), pinned by SHA-256 in catalog/finance-data-lock.json.

limitations: The protocol (optional rebalancing every 13 weeks with costs charged to the portfolio, free initial purchase, at most K stocks, pure tracking without an excess-return objective) differs from Beasley et al.'s single-rebalance model with a cost budget, so their published tracking errors are not directly comparable.
Weekly prices of 1992-1997 for constituents at the end of the sample; survivorship and constituent changes are not modelled, and dividends are ignored as in the OR-Library data.
The out-of-sample period (145 weeks) is public and short; candidates tuned on it overfit, and tracking errors from one period have wide sampling uncertainty.

The candidate runs in a sandboxed child process that never receives later data, realised outcomes or reference solutions, and no statement of the candidate is executed in the evaluator's process; outside macOS (kernel sandbox) deliberately hostile native code could bypass the file policy.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Replicate the returns of a stock index with a small number of its constituents while limiting transaction costs.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Passive index funds manage a large share of equity assets; holding few stocks lowers costs but creates tracking error, and selecting them is a hard cardinality-constrained optimization problem.
